events.title: Bluey’s Big Play
events.loc: The 5th Avenue Theatre , 1308 Fifth Ave., Seattle
events.desc: The Heeler family has saved me more than once, so you can consider me a “Bluey” fan for life. This live theater show brings larger-than-life puppets and master puppeteers to the stage. From that magic xylophone to adorable gnomes, it’s a chance to experience the usual shenanigans in a brand-new way (rather than, say, watching all 154 episodes again).

events.title: Spooky Science at the Burke Museum
events.cost: Included with admission ($16–$24); ages 3 and younger are free
events.loc: Burke Museum , 4303 Memorial Way N.E., Seattle
events.desc: Spooky, scary … stuffed animals? Head to the Burke Museum for creepy, crawly science activities all month long! On the second floor, you’ll find ways to piece together stuffed animal body parts and even craft your own bat to take home. On the third floor, you’ll discover glowing minerals and scary creatures.

events.title: Tacoma Honk Fest
events.loc: McKinley Hill Business District , McKinley Avenue and East Division Lane, Tacoma
events.desc: The absolute joy of Honk! Fest is undeniable. Drum lines, marching bands, brass bands and more take to the streets for a full day of music. Groove alongside them, check out the community booths, snag some merch and have a blast.

events.title: Kelsey Creek Farm Fair
events.cost: Many free activities; select activities have a small fee
events.loc: Kelsey Creek Farm , 410 130 Pl. S.E., Bellevue
events.desc: Ready for a fun fall day on the farm? This beloved community event gives kids a chance to meet farm animals, take a tractor-pulled wagon ride and explore a pumpkin patch. Snack on kettle corn or grab lunch from one of the food trucks and make a day of it!

events.title: Ching Garden Grand Opening
events.loc: Ching Garden , 16034 Greenwood Ave. N., Shoreline
events.desc: This sweet community garden honoring the Ching family has been in the works for a few years, and it is finally opening to the public! Hear the story behind the food forest, take a tour, and even take home some perennials and seeds. There will be kids activities too.

events.title: Fiesta del Maíz
events.desc: Celebrate Mesoamerican Indigenous cultures at this free fiesta. Special presentations bring history and traditions to life, and you can expect to learn traditional ways to cultivate and prepare corn. There will also be dance performances, colorful artwork, storytelling, crafts and more to enjoy.

events.title: Little Beats Concert Series
events.loc: McGilvra Elementary School , 1617 38th Ave. E., Seattle
events.desc: This little concert series is back for its third season! It kicks off on Saturday with Brian and the Good Buddies, so put on your dancing shoes and get ready to sing along. (And mark your calendars for Highlight Quartet on Nov. 7 and The Harmonica Pocket on Feb. 6.)

events.title: Issaquah Salmon Days
events.loc: Historic Shell Station & Downtown Issaquah , 232 Front St. N., Issaquah
events.desc: This beloved local festival kicks off on Saturday morning with a grand parade, and then a flurry of festivities continues through the weekend. You can expect DockDogs performances, arts and crafts, inflatables, mini golf and more activities, all in celebration of the triumphant salmon that have returned for the season.

events.title: Pumpkin Chomp & Stomp
events.cost: Included with admission ($17–$32; ages 2 and younger free) or membership
events.loc: Northwest Trek Wildlife Park , 11610 Trek Dr. E., Eatonville
events.desc: My daughter loved seeing animals snack on pumpkins last year at Northwest Trek , and we can’t wait to visit again this fall. The annual Pumpkin Chomp & Stomp includes special keeper chats and pumpkin treats for the otters and raccoons and bears (oh my!). Wear your costumes, walk the trails and enjoy the incredible park. Just plan for extra time on the playground.

events.title: Oktoberfest Kid’s Day
events.loc: Ounces Taproom & Beer Garden , 3809 Delridge Way S.W., Seattle
events.desc: One of our favorite breweries invites the whole family to get into the Oktoberfest spirit with fun activities. Kids can craft a pretzel necklace, compete in a coloring contest and get their face painted. Plus, the brewery is putting a twist on the classic game of Hammerschlagen — with pumpkins.
